messages.subject: Re: MSstats normalization
messages.body_plain:
Dear Gene,

Thank you for your question.
1. to turn off the normalization, use 'normalization=FALSE' As you mentioned, if you already external normalization function in log2 scale, 'normalization=FALSE' will not do anything for normalization, just will reformat for fitting the model next step.
2. about log transformation : MSstats now has only two possibility for log transformation, logTrans=2 or 10. Now logTrans=FALSE is not available. I will update it soon. If you want to use before I update, there is the temporary solution. After you applied an external normalization function, 'Intensity' column has normalization and log2 scaled values. Then please just recalculate 2^(Intensity) in 'Intensity' column. below is the simple code for that.

------------------------
## I assume the name of raw file is 'Msstats.input.annotate'
Msstats.input.annotate$Intensity<-2^(MSstats.input.annotate$Intensity)
data1<-dataProcess(Msstats.input.annotate, normalization=FALSE)
------------------------

I hope it will help for you.

Thanks,
Meena

messages.subject: Feature Selection
messages.body_plain:
Hello,
I was just wondering how the FeatureSelection in the dataProcess function is performed. What do the lambda and eta values stand for? when will there be more options released?

furthermore, I was wondering if one could normalize across the median intensities of all endogenous signals (when measuring a larger number of proteins in total) instead of using some selected standard proteins (how can we make sure that some housekeeping genes are not changing). I am just worried about artefacts due to an uneven loaded sample amount (total protein mass), which is usually determined by assays such as Lowry, Bradford or BCA, that are often not particularly accurate.

Thank you!

messages.body_plain:
Hello members of MSstats group,

I work with DDA spectra in label free, and
I found the R code using with MSstats for GroupComparison function,
but the function fit.model or fit.model.single are hidden functions.

I would know if it is possible to know, how the Fold Change (Log2FC) is measured ?
Is it a mean of the FC of all features for a protein?
Does the P.value take into account if there is a percentage of the features number by protein that have a significative fold change? or not?
Does the P.value take into account the abundance standard deviation between run ?

Thanks in advance for your answer.

Regards

Chloé
